properties.summary: A visible absorption maximum at 341 nm is attributed to charge transfer from SePh or selenide to Sm(III); comparison with compound 2 suggests selenide-to-Sm(III) charge transfer.

source_locations.location: main text, compound 1 discussion and Figure 1
main text, compound 1 discussion and comparison with compound 2

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Eight seven-coordinate Sm(III) ions occupy the vertices of a cube. Six selenide ions cap its faces, twelve bridging SePh ligands span its edges, and each Sm also binds one THF ligand.

synthesis.procedure: Sm was reacted with diphenyl diselenide in THF to form Sm(SePh)2, followed initially by reaction with elemental Se to obtain compound 1. A later, cleaner route prepared Sm(SePh)2 in THF and allowed it to decompose thermally at room temperature without added chalcogen.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature for the thermal decomposition route
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reaction followed by crystallization; alternatively, thermal decomposition of Sm(SePh)2
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Deep orange, air-sensitive crystals were obtained.

properties.summary: The visible spectrum is reported as featureless, in contrast to compound 1.

main text, comparison of visible spectra of compounds 1 and 2

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The seven Sm(III) ions of the cation form two square pyramids sharing a Sm3 face. Four μ3-sulfides and two μ5-sulfides cap external faces, while one μ4-sulfide bridges two reentrant Sm3 faces. Each Sm binds a chelating DME ligand. The crystal also contains a separate [Hg3(SePh)7]− anion and DME solvate.

synthesis.procedure: Sm(SePh)3, prepared by reducing diphenyl diselenide with Sm/Hg amalgam, was treated by slow addition of sulfur in DME. Addition of less than a full equivalent of sulfur gave compound 2.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: A yellow solid precipitated; light yellow, air-sensitive crystals were isolated.

title: Unexpected Synthetic Routes to Lanthanide Chalcogenido Clusters: Sm8Se6(SePh)12(THF)8 and [Sm7S7(SePh)6(DME)7]+
